correctness.rationale: The lower-bound mechanism is sound at the stated asymptotic level. Individualizing every gadget on the middle wall row fixes that separator pointwise, but deleting the row leaves a top strip A of treewidth Theta(n). Standard CFI twist mobility can be restricted to paths wholly inside A, so a robber strategy against K cops in A yields a Duplicator strategy for the corresponding fixed-K bijective pebble game while leaving the individualized row untouched. Since tw(A)=Theta(n), this gives an Omega(n) WL-dimension lower bound in the wall-side parameter. The small scripts are correctly presented only as structural examples; the asymptotic conclusion rests on the analytic treewidth/CFI argument.

originality.rationale: The core theorem is a direct localization of the classical CFI/treewidth/cops correspondence. Modern expositions explicitly identify moving the CFI twist with the robber and fixing origins of pebbled vertices with cop-occupied vertices. Once the individualized row is deleted and one observes that a remaining component still has linear treewidth, the claimed lower bound follows by applying that standard machinery inside that component. The exact phrase 'row individualization' may be new, but the mathematical mechanism is an immediate separator-plus-CFI corollary rather than a new lower-bound technique.

scientific_value.rationale: The example is a useful warning that individualizing a large separator does not help when a high-treewidth CFI region survives, but it does not develop a general theorem characterizing which individualization sets reduce WL dimension, nor a new cops/robber invariant. It therefore adds limited research value beyond the existing CFI/treewidth framework.
